verdict: Reddit's revenue grew 68% to $585M as ad sales jumped 74% — and with costs growing far more slowly, net income rose more than five-fold to $163M, 28 cents of every revenue dollar.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads shown across Reddit's communities — powered by more users, more time on site, and better ad targeting.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Mostly data licensing — deals that let AI companies train on Reddit's public posts — plus Reddit Premium subscriptions.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the product and the ad platform — up 18% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning advertisers and users — up 73% YoY, the fastest-growing cost line.

takeaways.title: Growth stayed hot
takeaways.text: Revenue growth hit 68%, powered by advertising (+74%) as daily users reached 116.0M, up 19% — Reddit is still getting bigger and better at selling ads against its communities.

takeaways.title: Profit rose five-fold
takeaways.text: Net income rose from $30M a year ago to $163M — 28% of revenue. Operating income was $139M, versus just $7M a year ago, because costs grew far more slowly than revenue.

takeaways.title: Cash flow followed
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $183M — 31% of revenue — on operating cash flow of $185M.

otherDetail: Other income of $22M, net — mostly interest earned on Reddit's cash and marketable securities — plus a small $2M tax benefit: Reddit's tax line was slightly negative this quarter, so it is counted here and the tax step reads $0.
footerNote: Figures are from Reddit's Q3 2025 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q; the advertising/other revenue split is from the 10-Q. Reddit's tax line was a $2M benefit this quarter; it is folded into other income so the chart's tax step reads $0.
